advisory, non-blocking per Step 1.65 WARN-first contract

BUILD/PROOF SANDBOX. The shared checkout does not compile: a peer's uncommitted WIP (src/pipeline/scope-binding.ts, 2 TS2488 errors, plus framework detectors and 5 test files) is mid-edit, and tsconfig sets noEmitOnError:true so no dist can be produced. Touching another agent's WIP is out of bounds (file-partition), so every build, test, and parity proof for this WO runs in a DETACHED-HEAD git worktree at C:/Users/willh/AppData/Local/Temp/crsb containing HEAD + exactly this WO's files (synced by scratchpad/sync-sandbox.sh). Clean HEAD builds there with exit 0, which is what proves the breakage is peer WIP and not this WO. Edits and commits still land in the main checkout on main. Sandbox needed a short path (Windows MAX_PATH) and staged copies of ASSISTANT/STANDARDS/layers.json + the analyze-coderef-semantics SKILL.md, which the header tests resolve relative to cwd's parent.

A new edge kind must be taught FIVE enumerations, not the two the plan's DL-2 named: graph-builder EdgeRelationship, graph-exporter ExportedGraphEdgeRelationship, output-validator VALID_RELATIONSHIPS (a RUNTIME GI-4 gate that failed the populate, not just a type), canonical-graph DEPENDS, mcp/graph-tools DEPENDS_KINDS. Only the last two are compile-checked-adjacent; the validator one fails at scan time.

'references' deliberately EXCLUDED from the DEPENDS traversal sets on both adjacency indexes. It targets ordinary code elements, so walking it would change what impact_of returns for every symbol any doc mentions - not additive. Exposed instead via a dedicated CanonicalGraphQuery.docReferences() accessor. 'contains' IS in DEPENDS: it can only land on doc nodes, so it cannot perturb an element-to-element answer. FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE: operator may rule on widening DEPENDS once real doc-impact data exists.
